glossary.Public health authorities: Organisations responsible for protecting the health of the whole population, such as UKHSA.
glossary.Encephalitis: Inflammation of the brain tissue, usually from a viral infection.
glossary.Acute meningitis: Sudden inflammation of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord.
glossary.Acute infective hepatitis: Sudden liver inflammation caused by an infection, usually a virus.
glossary.Herpes simplex: A virus causing cold sores and genital ulcers.
glossary.Syphilis: A sexually transmitted infection caused by Treponema pallidum.
glossary.HIV: Human immunodeficiency virus, which destroys CD4 T cells.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination before test results.
glossary.Formal notification: Officially reporting a suspected case to public health using the set form.
glossary.Lab confirmation: Proof of the infection by a laboratory test.
glossary.Antivirals: Drugs that stop a virus replicating.
glossary.Infection control: Measures such as isolation, hand hygiene and PPE to stop spread.
glossary.Close contacts: People who spent enough time near the patient to be at risk of catching the infection.
glossary.Catch-up vaccination: Giving missed vaccine doses to people who were not fully immunised.
glossary.Legislation: Laws passed by government; here the Health Protection Regulations.
glossary.Outbreak control: Actions taken to stop an outbreak spreading further.
glossary.Notification timeframe: The deadline within which a suspected case must be reported.
